entry: Jamaican black nationalist, Pan-Africanist activist and orator. Garvey founded the Universal Negro Improvement Association (UNIA) in Jamaica in 1914 and built its membership after moving to New York City in 1916. He promoted racial separatism, economic self-reliance and the Back-to-Africa movement; his ideas became known as Garveyism. His Black Star Line shipping company, launched in 1919, sold stock to supporters. In 1923 Garvey was convicted of mail fraud over those sales and imprisoned, a charge many contemporaries viewed as politically motivated. He was deported to Jamaica in 1927 and founded the People's Political Party in 1929. In 1964 his body was returned to Jamaica for reburial, and he was the first person formally recognized as a National Hero. His links with the [[Ku Klux Klan|Ku Klux Klan]] and his prejudice against Jews and mixed-race people drew criticism from many in the African diaspora. His ideas influenced [[Rastafari|Rastafarianism]] and the [[Nation of Islam]].

Roman general and statesman of the late Republic. Often called "the richest man in Rome," Crassus amassed a large fortune through property speculation during [[Sulla|Sulla's]] dictatorship and through silver mines. He rose to prominence by defeating the slave revolt led by [[Spartacus]] and shared the consulship with his rival [[Pompey]] in 70 BC. He joined [[Julius Caesar]] and Pompey in the First Triumvirate, an unofficial alliance that dominated Roman politics. As governor of Syria he invaded [[Parthian Empire|Parthia]] in 53 BC; his army was defeated at the Battle of Carrhae, and he was killed. His death ended the balance between Caesar and Pompey, and within four years Caesar crossed the Rubicon and began a civil war against Pompey.

Holiday on the day before Ash Wednesday, the last day of [[Carnival]]. Mardi Gras is French for "Fat Tuesday," marking the final day of eating rich foods before the Lenten fast. Also called Shrove Tuesday, it is known in the [[United Kingdom]] as Pancake Day, when pancakes use up eggs, milk and butter before Lent. In [[New Orleans]], [[Louisiana]], the Carnival season begins on January 6 and peaks on Fat Tuesday with parades, masked balls and king cake.

Canadian novelist, poet and literary critic. Since 1961 she has published 18 books of poetry, 18 novels, 11 books of nonfiction and nine collections of short fiction. Her best-known work is the dystopian novel *The Handmaid's Tale* (1985), set in a theocratic regime that subjugates women. Her writing addresses gender, Canadian identity, [[Religion|religion]] and [[Myth|myth]], the power of language, [[Climate change|climate change]] and [[Genetic engineering|genetic engineering]]. She has won two [[Booker Prize|Booker Prizes]] and numerous other awards, and many of her works have been adapted for film and television. Atwood co-founded the Griffin Poetry Prize and the Writers' Trust of Canada, and she is a senior fellow of Massey College in [[Toronto]]. She also invented the LongPen, a device for remote robotic writing of documents.

Australian former tennis player and Pentecostal minister. Court won 24 women's singles major titles, the most in women's tennis history, and 64 major titles in all, including 19 women's doubles and 21 mixed doubles titles. She won the first of seven consecutive Australian Open singles titles in 1960 and completed the singles [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] in 1970 by winning all four major titles. She retired in 1977 after taking breaks to have children. Court became associated with Pentecostalism in the 1970s, became a Christian minister in 1991 and founded Margaret Court Ministries. She has argued that children benefit from both maternal and paternal influences and has opposed [[Same-sex marriage|same-sex marriage]]. Her views have made her a polarizing figure in Australia, and proposals to rename the Margaret Court Arena have been debated.

Queen regnant of Denmark, Norway and Sweden from the late 1380s until her death, and founder of the Kalmar Union, which joined the [[Scandinavia|Scandinavian]] kingdoms for over a century. The youngest daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark, she married Haakon VI in 1363 at age ten and was queen consort of Norway until 1380. After the deaths of her husband and son, she was proclaimed queen of the Scandinavian kingdoms. She intended to unite Scandinavia against the power of the [[Hanseatic League]]. She was succeeded by her grandnephew, Erik of Pomerania, who came of age in 1401, but she remained sole ruler in all but name until her death, and her subjects called her "Lady King." Some Norwegian and Swedish historians criticize her for favoring Denmark and for autocratic rule. She is generally thought to have been highly regarded in Norway and respected in Denmark and Sweden.

American cultural anthropologist, author and speaker who became prominent in the mass media. Her first ethnography, *Coming of Age in Samoa* (1928), addressed adolescence and sexuality and catapulted her to national visibility. Her book *Sex and Temperament in Three Primitive Societies* (1935) examined gender roles based on fieldwork in [[Papua New Guinea]]. Mead studied with [[Franz Boas]] at [[Columbia University]] and was curator of ethnology at the [[American Museum of Natural History]] from 1946 to 1969. Her reports on sexual attitudes in Pacific and Southeast Asian cultures influenced the [[Sexual revolution]] of the 1960s, and her association with cultural relativism drew sharp criticism from conservatives. Anthropologist Derek Freeman later challenged her Samoan findings, while others defended her framework. Mead served as president of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 1975.

American birth control activist, sex educator, writer and nurse. Sanger opened the first birth control clinic in the United States and founded Planned Parenthood. Working as a nurse in New York City's slums, she campaigned to legalize [[Birth control|contraception]] on the ground that women should decide if and when to have children. She was arrested eight times for distributing information about contraceptives. Court rulings that followed her activism legalized birth control, including *Griswold v. Connecticut*, which legalized contraception without a prescription for couples nationwide. As an adherent of [[Eugenics|eugenics]], she argued that birth control would reduce the number of unfit people; her eugenics views remain controversial. Sanger discouraged abortion, and her clinics never offered abortion services during her lifetime. In the early 1950s she persuaded philanthropists to fund biologist Gregory Pincus's development of the first birth control pill.

British Conservative politician and prime minister of the United Kingdom from 1979 to 1990. She was the first woman to hold the office and the longest-serving British prime minister of the 20th century. As leader of the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] from 1975 to 1990, she pursued policies known as Thatcherism, including privatization and curbs on trade unions. Victory in the [[Falklands War]] in 1982 and an economic recovery brought a landslide in 1983 after early unpopularity. Her support for the Community Charge, or poll tax, was widely unpopular, and her Eurosceptic views were not shared by others in her cabinet. She resigned in 1990 after a leadership challenge and was succeeded by [[John Major]]. After leaving the House of Commons in 1992, she was given a life peerage and sat in the [[House of Lords]]. A polarizing figure, she is nonetheless viewed favorably in historical rankings of British prime ministers.

Spread, usually made from vegetable oil, used as a substitute for butter. Margarine is a water-in-fat emulsion used for flavoring, baking and cooking. The name combines Latin *oleum* ("olive oil") and Greek *margarite* ("pearl"). Responding to a challenge from [[Napoleon III]], Hippolyte Mège-Mouriès invented margarine in 1869 from beef tallow. He sold the patent in 1871 to the Dutch company Jurgens, later part of [[Unilever]]. Dairy interests opposed margarine, and the 1886 Margarine Act imposed prohibitive taxes in the United States. Hydrogenated vegetable oils became the main ingredient after shortages of beef fat, and by 1950 U.S. manufacturers had switched almost entirely to vegetable oils. Partially hydrogenated oils, which produce trans fats linked to cardiovascular disease, have since been restricted in many countries.

Canadian-American actress and activist. Born in Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Kidder is best known for playing Lois Lane in the *Superman* films (1978–1987) opposite [[Christopher Reeve]]. She won the Saturn Award for Best Actress for *Superman* and also starred in the horror films *Black Christmas* (1974) and *The Amityville Horror* (1979). A manic episode in 1996 stemmed from [[Bipolar disorder|bipolar disorder]], and she continued in independent films and television afterward. She was an outspoken political, environmental and antiwar activist.

Australian actress and film producer. Robbie began on the soap opera *Neighbours* and gained international recognition in Martin Scorsese's *The Wolf of Wall Street* (2013). She played Harley Quinn in the DC Extended Universe films and received [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations for Best Actress for *I, Tonya* (2017) and Best Supporting Actress for *Bombshell* (2019). Her highest-grossing film, *Barbie* (2023), earned her a Best Picture nomination as a producer. She co-founded the production company LuckyChap Entertainment with her husband, Tom Ackerley, in 2014 and is an advocate for human rights and gender equality.

American-born Greek soprano and one of the most influential opera singers of the 20th century. Critics praised her bel canto technique and dramatic interpretations, and she was known as "La Divina" ("The Divine One"). Born in Manhattan to Greek immigrant parents, she trained in Greece and established her career in Italy. Her repertoire ranged from bel canto operas by Bellini, Donizetti and Rossini to works by Verdi and Puccini. She performed 180 times across 22 operas at La Scala in Milan between 1950 and 1962 and recorded extensively for EMI. Leonard Bernstein called her "the Bible of opera." Vocal challenges led to her gradual retirement from the stage by 1965. Her widely publicized relationship with shipping magnate [[Aristotle Onassis]] overshadowed her later years. Her ashes were scattered over the [[Aegean Sea]] in 1979.

Italian physician and educator known for her writing on scientific pedagogy and for the Montessori method of education. She was one of the first women to attend medical school in Italy, graduating with honors from the [[Sapienza University of Rome]] in 1896. Her interest in child development grew from work with children with intellectual disabilities in psychiatric clinics. In 1907 she opened the first Casa dei Bambini ("Children's House") in Rome's San Lorenzo district, applying her method to ordinary preschool children. Her approach, which emphasizes independence, sensory learning and prepared environments, spread across Europe, the Americas and Asia through training courses, books and schools. Critics argue that it gives insufficient emphasis to structured academic instruction, and empirical studies show mixed outcomes compared with conventional schooling.

Habsburg monarch, the only woman to rule the Habsburg monarchy in her own right. Maria Theresa reigned from 1740 until her death in 1780 as sovereign of Austria, Hungary, Bohemia and other territories, and was Holy Roman Empress by marriage. She inherited the lands under the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 from her father, Charles VI. Prussia under [[Frederick the Great]] seized [[Silesia]] during the War of the Austrian Succession (1740–1748), and she never regained it. She introduced institutional, financial, medical and educational reforms, reorganized the army and promoted commerce and agriculture, ruling as an autocrat with the counsel of advisers. A pious [[Catholic Church|Catholic]], she despised Freemasons, Jews and Protestants and on occasion ordered their expulsion. She bore 16 children who survived infancy, including [[Joseph II]] and [[Marie Antoinette]].

American singer-songwriter and record producer, known for her five-octave range and whistle register. She was the only artist whose first five singles all reached number one in the United States, and she has the most Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles of any solo artist (19). Her holiday single "All I Want for Christmas Is You," from *Merry Christmas* (1994), is the best-selling holiday single by a woman. She has won five [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards]] and served as a judge on *American Idol* in 2013. *Rolling Stone* ranked her the fifth-greatest singer of all time in 2023.

Archipelago of mostly dormant volcanic islands in the western [[Pacific Ocean]], part of [[Micronesia]]. The islands are divided between the U.S. territory of [[Guam]] and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. Chamorro people settled the islands, possibly after making the longest uninterrupted ocean voyage in human history. Spanish expeditions, beginning with one led by [[Ferdinand Magellan]], were the first Europeans to arrive, and the islands were named after Queen Mariana of Austria. Spain colonized the islands in the 17th century; Germany and Japan later controlled them. U.S. forces invaded in 1944. The economy relies heavily on [[Tourism|tourism]] and the U.S. military.

Deepest oceanic trench on Earth, a crescent-shaped depression in the western Pacific Ocean about 200 km east of the [[Mariana Islands]]. It measures about 2,550 km long and 69 km wide. Its deepest point, the [[Challenger Deep]] at the southern end of the trench, has a maximum known depth of 10,935 meters, more than 2 km farther from sea level than the peak of [[Mount Everest]]. The water pressure at the bottom is 111 MPa (16,100 psi), approximately 1,100 times the standard atmospheric pressure at sea level. The trench forms where the Pacific plate is subducted beneath the Mariana plate, reflecting [[Plate tectonics|plate tectonics]]. Single-celled organisms have been recorded at a depth of 10.6 km (35,000 ft). In 2009 the United States established the Mariana Trench Marine National Monument, which excludes Challenger Deep.

Queen consort of France from 1774 to 1792 as the wife of [[Louis XVI]], and the last queen before the monarchy was abolished during the [[French Revolution]]. Born in [[Vienna]], she was the youngest daughter of [[Maria Theresa]] and Francis I, Holy Roman Emperor. She was betrothed to the dauphin Louis-Auguste in 1769 to strengthen the Franco-Austrian alliance, and they married in 1770. Blamed for the nation's financial crisis, she was nicknamed "Madame Déficit." She was falsely accused of defrauding the Crown's jewelers in the Affair of the Diamond Necklace, but the accusations still damaged her reputation. After the royal family was imprisoned in 1792, she was convicted of high treason and executed by [[Guillotine|guillotine]] in 1793.

American actress and model, one of the most popular sex symbols of the 1950s and early 1960s and an emblem of the era's [[Sexual revolution|sexual revolution]]. Known for comic "blonde bombshell" roles, she starred in 1953 in *Niagara* and the comedies *Gentlemen Prefer Blondes* and *How to Marry a Millionaire*, which established her star image as a "dumb blonde." Her nude images appeared on the first issue of [[Playboy]] that year. Feeling typecast and underpaid by the studio, she founded her own production company, and her later films included *The Seven Year Itch* (1955) and *Some Like It Hot* (1959), for which she won a Golden Globe. Her marriages to [[Joe DiMaggio]] and playwright [[Arthur Miller]] ended in divorce. Her death from a barbiturate overdose was ruled a probable suicide.

Serbian conceptual and performance artist, who calls herself the "grandmother of performance art." Her work explores body art, endurance, the relationship between performer and audience, and the limits of the body. Born in [[Belgrade]], she worked with the German artist Ulay on relational pieces, including walking the length of the [[Great Wall of China]] before their separation. Her 2010 retrospective *The Artist Is Present* at the [[Museum of Modern Art]] had her sit silently opposite visitors for up to 736 hours over three months. In 2007 she founded the Marina Abramović Institute, a nonprofit foundation for performance art.

French lawyer and politician who led the far-right National Rally from 2011. The party was formerly known as the National Front. She ran for the French presidency in 2012, 2017 and 2022, reaching the runoff in 2017 and 2022 against [[Emmanuel Macron]]. Under her leadership the party softened some positions while retaining strong anti-immigration, [[Nationalism|nationalist]] and protectionist policies. She has been a member of the National Assembly since 2017. In 2025 she was convicted of misusing European Parliament funds; the conviction was upheld on appeal, and she maintains the case is politically motivated.

Organisms that live in salt water, including seawater and brackish coastal habitats. Marine life spans microorganisms such as [[Bacteria|bacteria]] and plankton, [[Algae|algae]], and animals from invertebrates to [[Whale|whales]] and [[Shark|sharks]]. As of 2023, more than 242,000 marine species had been documented, and perhaps two million remain to be documented. Researchers describe about 2,300 new species each year. By volume, oceans provide about 90% of the living space on Earth. The earliest known life forms evolved in the [[Archean]] oceans around deep-sea [[Hydrothermal vent|hydrothermal vents]]. Marine primary producers, mainly [[Cyanobacteria|cyanobacteria]] and chloroplastic algae, produce oxygen through [[Photosynthesis|photosynthesis]]. Marine vertebrates include fish, marine mammals, reptiles and seabirds.

Fictional video game character and mascot of [[Nintendo]]. Created by [[Shigeru Miyamoto]], Mario first appeared as the player character of the 1981 platform game *Donkey Kong*. He is an Italian-American plumber who lives in the Mushroom Kingdom with his younger twin brother, Luigi, and usually rescues Princess Peach from the villain Bowser. Miyamoto created the character after Nintendo was unable to license [[Popeye]] as the protagonist. Mario became the star of the *Super Mario* platform series with *Super Mario Bros.* (1985) for the [[Nintendo Entertainment System]]. He has appeared in hundreds of games, including the *Mario Kart* racing series and sports titles, and the Mario franchise is the best-selling video game franchise of all time.

Peruvian novelist, journalist, essayist and politician, and one of the leading writers of the Latin American Boom. His novels include *The Time of the Hero* (1963), *The Green House* (1965) and *Conversation in the Cathedral* (1969), which portray power, corruption and authoritarianism in Peruvian and Latin American society. He won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Literature for his "cartography of structures of power." Vargas Llosa first supported the Cuban government of [[Fidel Castro]] but later identified as a classical liberal with anti-left views, particularly after the imprisonment of poet Heberto Padilla in 1971. He ran for president of Peru in 1990 as the candidate of the center-right Democratic Front, losing to [[Alberto Fujimori]]. He was elected to the Académie Française in 2021.
